title: Hierarchical role constraints and audit stream integrity workstream
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: We are implementing a focused workstream to (1) codify hierarchical role constraints for RBAC v2 to eliminate privilege escalation paths that surfaced in the third-party pen test, and (2) harden the audit stream so SAML/SSO events, elevated admin sessions, and policy changes are reliably captured, tamper-evident, and searchable in the observability stack.

Scope: This ticket covers threat modeling revisions, a prioritized remediation backlog from the pen-test report, new runtime checks and enforcement for hierarchical role boundaries, audit pipeline integrity checks (signing, ordering, replay-detection), and SAML assertion fidelity tests during admin flows. Work explicitly does NOT include UI re-skinning of the admin console; it does include telemetry hooks for Console and Dedicated control planes.

Goals and success criteria: 
- Define and land a formal hierarchical constraint grammar and enforcement layer for RBAC v2 that prevents privilege inheritance loops and disallows 'admin-of-admin' transitive grants by default.
- Automated integration tests proving that role modifications do not create new attack paths (negative tests); regression tests for existing role semantics (positive tests).
- Ensure 100% of SAML Admin SSO assertions are logged with a tamper-evident digest in the audit stream and cross-verified against the assertion ingestion pipeline within 60s.
- Add checksum and sequence validation to the audit-forwarder; detect and alert on missing or reordered audit batches.
- Complete pen-test remediation items triaged as high in the external report and move medium items to the next cycle.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Enforcement at the authorization service boundary (centralized) to avoid subtle drift between control planes; this increases single-service responsibility but simplifies auditability.
- Use HMAC-signed batch envelopes for audit forwarding rather than full blockchain or append-only store to balance operational complexity and timeliness. If needed, we can iterate to an append-only store in a follow-up.
- Start with a conservative hierarchical model (deny-by-default for transitive grants) to minimize risk; we will relax via explicit allow-rules only after formal review.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Threat model refresh and mapping of pen-test findings to technical remediation tasks (2 days).
2) Prototype hierarchical constraint checker and unit tests (5 days).
3) Instrument SAML assertion capture and attach digest metadata to audit events (3 days).
4) Bake audit-forwarder batch signing and sequence checks; integrate with Alerting (4 days).
5) End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout to staging Dedicated pool (3 days).
6) Documentation, runbook, and post-deploy regression eval prompt set (2 days).

Acceptance criteria: 
- PRs merged with green CI and no test regressions.
- Integration test demonstrating closed pen-test path scenarios.
- New alerts firing in staging when audit batches are dropped or signatures fail.
- Security review sign-off and one SRE on-call rotation trained on runbook.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Overly strict hierarchical rules may block legitimate admin workflows. Mitigation: provide an escape hatch via scoped override requests requiring two approvers and an audit trail.
- Risk: Signing audit envelopes adds latency. Mitigation: batch sign asynchronously and ensure ingestion checks are performant; measure P50/P95 latency impact.
- Risk: SAML assertion capture might miss transient flows in older clients. Mitigation: add an assertion re-ingest path and monitor mismatches between auth service logs and audit stream.

Follow-ups and related work: 
- Post-launch: evaluate moving from signed batches to an append-only store for high-sensitivity tenants.
- Cross-team: coordinate with Console (PM/UX) on admin workflow telemetry and with Dedicated infra for canary schedule.

Links and artifacts: 
- Pen-test report (redacted): https://drive.company.com/pen-test-2026-redacted
- Threat model doc: https://confluence.company.com/display/Sec/RBAC+v2+Threat+Model+2026-02
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/compare/feature/hierarchical-constraints
- Audit pipeline dashboard: https://grafana.company.com/d/abc123/audit-forwarder
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.company.com/display/Sec/Audit+Forwarder+Runbook

Notes for reviewers: Please focus review on the hierarchical constraint grammar and the negative test cases that represent realistic attacker paths, not hypothetical edge-cases. Also sanity-check the HMAC envelope format in the audit-forwarder PR for replay and ordering guarantees.
